questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The playground was way **__large then I had__** imagined, and in cleaning it, my back began to ache.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is "larger than I had."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When two items/people/situations are compared, a comparative degree is used by putting ‘er’ to the adjective word or "more" with the adjective in association with the word ‘than’.

 
 
• Example: 
 
• *She is more cheerful than her sister.*
 
• *She is smarter than her sister.*​
 
 
 
• Here, we need the comparative degree of the word 'large.'
 
• The comparative degree of 'large' is formed by adding "er" after the positive degree of the adjective "large."
 
• Therefore, the comparative degree of "large" is "larger."
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence__: *The playground was way __**larger than I had**__ imagined, and in cleaning it, my back began to ache.*

**Direction: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.**

__Shall you pass__ me that pasta bowl?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'​Can you pass****.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence needs improvement in the part **"Shall you pass."**
 
• Let us see the usage of the given modal verbs:​
 
 
• Shall: We use "shall" to make predictions and to state facts about the future. 
 
 
• Example: *We shall__ never forget the holiday we had in Vietnam.*
 
 
 
• *​*Can: We use "can" to talk about the ability to do something at a specific time in the present or future.
 __
 
• Example: *I can__ see you.*
 
 
 
• Could: When "could" is used as the past tense of "can", it refers to an ability that a person generally had in the past or to something that was generally possible in the past.
 __
 
• Example: *When I was younger, I could__ run for miles.*
 
 
 
 
 
• ​As the sentence is talking about the ability to pass her that pasta bowl, so we must use **"can"** in this sentence.
 
• The structure of an interrogative sentence with **"can"** is --->>> **Can + Subject + V1 + Object?**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 ​

Correct sentence:* **__**Can you pass**__ me that pasts bowl?*

questions.question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He had begun to dig / diligent along the / low tideline and had / captured two clams.
questions.solution:
Here the erroneous part is **"diligent along the."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part (diligent along the) of the sentence.
 
• The word "diligent" is an adjective.
 
• We need an adverb form of the word "diligent" to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• An adverb is a word that modifies (describes) a verb (he sings loudly), an adjective (very tall), another adverb (ended too quickly), or even a whole sentence.
 
• Adverbs often end in -ly, but some (such as fast) look exactly the same as their adjective counterparts. 
 
• The adverb form of "diligent" is "diligently."
 
• Therefore, the use of 'diligent' should be replaced with 'diligently' to modify the verb "dig" to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• So, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 ​

Correct sentence__: *He had begun to dig __**diligently along the**__ low tideline and had captured two clams.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I ______ your remaining project if you get groceries for me from the market.
questions.solution:
Here the correct part is "will do."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us see the meanings of the given options:
 
 
• **Would do: **We use "would" as the past of "will" and it is used to make hypotheses. In this condition, we imagine a situation.

 
 
• Example:* I **would do**__ your assignment, but my sister has an examination today.*
 
 
 
• **Will do:** We use** "will" **to express beliefs about the present or future, to talk about what people want to do or are willing to do, and to make promises, offers, and requests.
 __
 
• **Example: ***He **will do**__ this task if I can find his number.*
 
 
 
• **Will have done: **We use **"will have done"** when we are looking back from a point in time in the future.
 __
 
• **Example:** *By the end of the decade, scientists **will have done**__ this experiment.*
 
 
 
• **Would have done: **We use **"would have done"** as the past tense form of **"will have done."**
 __
 
• **Example:** *I phoned at six o'clock. I knew he **would have done**__ that work by then.*
 
 
 
 
 
• As the given sentence is referring to the willingness to do the remaining project, we must use **"will do"** in this case.
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 2.

 ​

__Correct sentence__: *I __**will do**__ your remaining project if you get groceries for me from the market.*

**Direction: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

A significant number of students volunteers each year for environmental projects.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The error lies in part 'volunteers each year for' of the sentence.
 
• The rule is- the expression 'a number of__' is always followed by a 'plural verb' 
 
• Example:- A number of people **have **written in about this subject.
 
• **In the given sentence the structure- '**__**A**__ significant __**number of'** __will follow the same rule.
 
• Therefore, the word "**volunteer**" would be the correct verb form in this case, matching the plurality of "**students**".*​​*
 
• ​​To make the sentence grammatically correct, we must substitute "volunteers" with "volunteer."
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 1.

__Correct sentence__: *A significant number of students __**volunteer each year for**__ environmental projects.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The expression** 'the number of' is **followed by a '**singular verb' **while the expression '**a number of' **is followed by a '**plural verb'.**
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• The number of people we need to hire **is **thirteen.
 
• A number of buildings around the Parliament **are **still smouldering today.
